About us

Our story

Our names are Spencer and Benedict McKay and we are brothers sailing together in the 49er class working towards the LA and Brisbane Olympics.

We have been sailing for most of our lives, after dad pushed us off the beach as soon as mum would agree. We both sailed on our own in the early years, with Spencer winning an Optimist State Championship and Benedict podiuming at multiple teams racing regattas and also being one of the youngest members in the NSWIS 420 squad.

After Spencer graduated from the Optimist, we decided to team up in the 420 halfway through 2021. We won our first regatta in the 420, winning every race. From there we went on to win three state titles and one youth national title in the 420. Competing at our first 420 World Championship in 2023, we took a race win on the tricky waters of Rio, and also finished top 10 in the South American 420 Championship.

At the same time, we were also competing for Cranbrook in the schools teams racing. Teaming up as skippers in the Cranbrook First VI, we won three state titles, along with a 1st and 2nd place at Teams Racing Nationals. After Benedict finished school, we moved into the 49er class, first stepping into the 49erFX which is the smaller version of the 49er, which allows lighter teams to be competitive. This provided us with a unique opportunity to sail against the top female skiff sailors in the country, and we placed 3rd at Sail Sydney in 2024.

With the goal of increasing our weight for the 49er (lucky us, not so great for Mum’s grocery bill!), by the start of 2025 we were heavy enough to jump into the bigger Olympic class boat. As the youngest team in the squad, we started training at the national training centre at Middle Harbour with the Australian Sailing Team. With a rigorous gym program and a strict on-water training schedule, our progress skyrocketed as we worked towards our first campaign overseas in 2026. We were proud to achieve 5th under 23 at the 49er Europeans (32nd overall) and 2nd Australian boat, demonstrating our potential as we work towards the 2032 Olympics.

Patrons program

Back the next Australian skiff

We are seeking a group of patrons to assist us financially as we progress in the class towards our Olympic goal. The Olympic standard for a successful campaign sees us travelling to Europe numerous times a year where we train and compete against the top sailors in the world in different events including sailing grand slams, Europeans, Junior Worlds and Open World championship events. It is at these events we check in to see where we are at in terms of our boat speed, racing skills and performance under pressure. In order to give ourselves the best opportunity to succeed, we also need to invest in multiple sets of sails per year, coaching, accommodation, and other boat parts/maintenance.

Given our results this year we plan to do a full year of racing abroad next year with our two key events being the Open Worlds and Junior World championships in July and August 2027. While we continue to self-fund our campaign, additional funding will allow us to take the next step in our development to become a dominant team on the Olympic sailing circuit.

We are so grateful for the opportunity we have to participate in this amazing sport, something we fully appreciate. We both try to give back to the sport everyday, coaching the future generation at our old school in the form of both coaching from the rib and jumping in the boat with junior sailors as well. We take great pride in trying to instil important values to the future generation to maintain the sportsmanship seen in the sport of sailing.

We would love for the opportunity to welcome patrons and supporters to our campaign support team as we build towards an Olympic medal. To create an Olympic medal standard campaign involves the help of many people that all play a genuine role in reaching the Olympics.

What patrons get

  • Daily email or WhatsApp updates direct from us while we're racing at major events — the honest version, not the press release
  • An invitation to come out on the water and watch us race here in Australia
  • Your name alongside the campaign as we build toward Brisbane 2032

Tax-deductible giving

Our campaign is registered with the Australian Sports Foundation under “49ers campaigning for Brisbane 2032”. Donations of $2 or more made through our ASF page are tax deductible in Australia, and the ASF issues your receipt.

Donate via the Australian Sports Foundation

Sponsorship arrangements, where a business receives advertising or branding in return, are not treated as donations. The ASF cannot provide tax advice — check with your own adviser or the ATO if you are unsure.
